introduction: At this level, we understand how scientists extract DNA from one organism and paste it into another, and how nanotechnology has created the super-materials of the future.

core_concepts.title: Genetic Engineering
core_concepts.description: The artificial manipulation, modification, and recombination of DNA to modify an organism. The newly formed DNA containing genes from two different sources is called **'Recombinant DNA (rDNA)'**.

core_concepts.title: GMO (Genetically Modified Organisms)
core_concepts.description:
Organisms whose genetic material has been altered using genetic engineering. 
1. **Bt Cotton:** The ONLY commercial GM crop cultivated in India. A gene from a soil bacterium called **'Bacillus thuringiensis'** is inserted into the cotton plant, making it naturally toxic to the deadly bollworm pest. 
2. **Golden Rice:** A genetically modified variety of rice heavily fortified with 'Beta-carotene', which the human body converts into **Vitamin A** (to fight childhood blindness).

core_concepts.title: Cloning
core_concepts.description:
The process of creating an exact, 100% identical genetic replica of a biological entity. 
**Dolly the Sheep:** She was the world's first mammal to be successfully cloned from an adult somatic cell (created by Ian Wilmut in 1996).

core_concepts.title: Miracle Nanomaterials
core_concepts.description:
1. **Graphene:** A single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a 2D honeycomb lattice. It is 200 times stronger than steel, incredibly lightweight, and the best known conductor of electricity. 
2. **Fullerene (Buckyball - C60):** A spherical molecule composed of exactly 60 carbon atoms, resembling a hollow soccer ball.

important_entities.name: The 'Bt' in Bt Cotton
important_entities.significance: Examiners frequently ask what 'Bt' stands for in Bt Cotton. Students instinctively tick 'Biotechnology', which is completely wrong. It stands for the name of the bacterium: **Bacillus thuringiensis**.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: In natural sexual reproduction, the offspring receives 50% DNA from the mother and 50% from the father, making it unique. However, 'Cloning' is an asexual process where **100% of the DNA** comes from a single parent, resulting in an identical twin.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Golden Rice has a golden-yellow color due to Beta-carotene, which provides Vitamin A. Vitamin A is crucial for good eyesight and preventing night blindness.

exam_strategy_tips: A favorite State PCS/UPSC question: 'Which is the only Genetically Modified (GM) crop approved for commercial cultivation in India?' Answer: Bt Cotton.
